sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to Parkinson’s Disease
sources.text: Bradykinesia: This slowed movement is the most noticeable of all the symptoms. Clients with PD have difficulties initiating movement, such as walking or getting up out of a chair. Bradykinesia may progress to akinesia, which is the inability to move. Also, clients usually present with an expressionless face or flat affect due to facial rigidity. Deep brain stimulation has been found to be effective in reducing tremors, bradykinesia, and rigidity. A pulse generator sends controlled electrical signals to electrodes surgically implanted in the brain.
